blocks.text: 1. Encoder-Decoder Architecture
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445740361-41303368.png

Teacher Forcing, the previous topic, covered a specific training technique for the decoder. Encoder-Decoder Architecture gives a complete, dedicated look at the structure previewed throughout this module, closing it with a unified picture.
It closes the Sequence Models module by formalizing the encoder and decoder into one complete system, explored in full depth throughout this final topic of the module.
2. Recapping What's Already Been Introduced

This connects back to the encoder-decoder structure previewed throughout Sequence-to-Sequence Learning and Teacher Forcing. Every piece of this architecture has genuinely already been introduced separately across those two prior topics.
This topic genuinely assembles them into one complete, unified picture, bringing together everything already covered piecemeal throughout the rest of this module.
3. The Encoder's Role
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445740362-783708690.png

This connects back to processing one time step at a time, already covered in Time Steps. The encoder genuinely reads the entire input sequence, one time step at a time, following that same sequential processing.
It produces the genuinely final context vector already covered in Sequence-to-Sequence Learning, the complete, compressed summary that gets handed off to the decoder.

blocks.text: 4. The Decoder's Role
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445740362-134051427.png

This connects back to the decoder starting from context, already covered in Sequence-to-Sequence Learning. The decoder genuinely takes that context vector and generates the output sequence, one time step at a time.
It uses Teacher Forcing, already covered in the previous topic, during training specifically, feeding the genuinely correct previous word at each step to keep training stable and efficient.
5. Two Genuinely Independent Components
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445740362-586544453.png

A genuinely important structural insight connects back to Network Architecture, already covered in its own topic. The encoder and decoder are genuinely separate components, each potentially built from genuinely different internal designs.
This structural independence, already covered in this section, is a genuinely deliberate design choice, distinguishing the encoder's own reading role from the decoder's own generating role.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: This structural independence, already covered in this topic, means the specific internal architecture used for the encoder does not need to match the specific internal architecture used for the decoder at all.

blocks.text: 6. Why Separating Them Genuinely Helps
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445740363-172334027.png

This connects forward to Transfer Learning, covered later in this course. Keeping the encoder and decoder genuinely separate lets each one be reused or swapped somewhat independently, a genuinely valuable practical benefit.
This is a genuinely useful, flexible property that becomes especially valuable in later, more advanced architectures, already covered as a forward-looking theme throughout the rest of this topic.
7. Recapping The Fixed-Size Bottleneck
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445740363-514040020.png

This connects back to the information bottleneck issue, already covered in Sequence-to-Sequence Learning. The plain encoder-decoder design, already covered throughout this topic, still genuinely inherits that same bottleneck.
This motivates Attention Mechanism, covered later in this course, as a genuinely direct enhancement, extending exactly the same encoder-decoder foundation already covered throughout this topic.

blocks.text: 8. Flexibility In The Building Blocks

A genuinely important, forward-looking observation connects forward to Recurrent Neural Networks, covered in the very next module. The encoder and decoder can genuinely each be built from different specific network types.

This genuinely flexible foundation, already covered in this section, is exactly why the encoder-decoder pattern, already covered throughout this topic, reappears across so many different architectures throughout the rest of this course.
9. Recognizing When The Plain Architecture Is Genuinely Sufficient

blocks.alt: Recognizing When The Plain Architecture Is Genuinely Sufficient
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445740364-677529813.png

This connects back to genuinely shorter sequences, where the information bottleneck, already covered, matters less. The plain architecture, already covered in this topic, often works genuinely well here.
Wanting a genuinely simple, foundational starting point before adding Attention is another genuine case where understanding this plain structure, already covered, is a genuinely necessary first step.
10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates a genuinely complete, minimal encoder-decoder pipeline in code, tying together every piece already covered throughout this module.

code.content:
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.RandomState(42)

def encoder(input_sequence, rng):
    # already covered as the encoder's own role in this topic: reading input, one time step at a time
    hidden_state = np.zeros(8)
    for word in input_sequence:
        hidden_state = hidden_state * 0.5 + rng.normal(size=8) * 0.1  # a genuinely simplified update rule
    return hidden_state  # already covered as the context vector

def decoder(context_vector, max_length, rng):
    # already covered as the decoder's own role in this topic: generating output, one time step at a time
    output_words = []
    vocabulary = ["le", "chat", "dort", "END"]
    state = context_vector.copy()
    for t in range(max_length):
        word_index = int(abs(state[0] * 10)) % len(vocabulary)
        word = vocabulary[word_index]
        if word == "END":
            break
        output_words.append(word)
        state = state * 0.9 + rng.normal(size=8) * 0.05
    return output_words

input_sequence = ["the", "cat", "sleeps"]
context = encoder(input_sequence, rng)  # already covered as the encoder's own role in this topic
output_sequence = decoder(context, max_length=6, rng=rng)  # already covered as the decoder's own role in this topic

print(f"Input sequence ({len(input_sequence)} time steps): {' '.join(input_sequence)}")
print(f"Context vector shape (already covered in this topic): {context.shape}")
print(f"Output sequence ({len(output_sequence)} time steps): {' '.join(output_sequence)}")

blocks.text: 11. Sequence Models: Module Complete

items: Encoder-Decoder Architecture formalizes the encoder and decoder into one complete system.
The encoder reads the entire input sequence, one time step at a time, producing a context vector.
The decoder generates the output sequence from that context vector, one time step at a time.
The encoder and decoder are genuinely separate, independent components with potentially different designs.
This independence allows each component to be reused or swapped somewhat independently.
The plain design still inherits the information bottleneck, motivating Attention Mechanism as an enhancement.
The encoder and decoder can each be built from different specific network types.
